item.title: A Tutorial on Future Vehicular Communications: From Performance Metrics to Open Research Directions
item.description: The study of vehicular networks has evolved into a new era thanks to rapid advances in electric, transportation, communication, and automobile technologies. However, the realization of modern applications like autonomous driving, intelligent transportation systems, and the smart city remain a major challenge due to the high requirements for performance metrics like data rate, latency, reliability, connectivity, coverage, and security. Moreover, in vehicular network, the performance metrics are not independent and may have a complex coupling relationship, i.e., optimizing one may result in degrading others. In this paper, we begin with discussing the coupling effect among the aforementioned performance metrics, aiming to provide a basic concept of the challenges of future vehicular networks. We aim to provide a comprehensive review of recent developments in vehicular communication technologies, such as the fifth-generation new radio (5G NR), dedicated short-range communications (DSRC), millimeter wave/terahertz communications, mobile edge computing (MEC), integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted vehicular networks, and blockchain-assisted security. The paper also covers the role of AI and its impact on the performance of each of the aforementioned applications. We then summarize several promising areas that can influence the future research in vehicular networks. Lastly, the paper concludes by highlighting key research challenges and future directions in the domain of vehicular networks.
item.authors: Junliang Ye;Xiaohu Ge;Yuxi Zhao;Yue Yu;Hamid Gharavi;

item.title: Edge Case Detection in Automated Driving: Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions
item.description: Automated vehicles (AVs) promise to enhance transportation safety and efficiency. However, ensuring their reliability in real-world conditions remains challenging, particularly due to rare and unexpected situations known as edge cases. While numerous approaches exist for detecting edge cases, a comprehensive survey reviewing these techniques is lacking. This paper bridges this gap by presenting a hierarchical review and systematic classification of edge case detection and assessment methodologies. Our classification is structured on two levels: first, by AV modules, including perception and trajectory-related (encompassing prediction, planning, and control) subsystems; and second, by underlying methodologies and theories guiding these techniques. Furthermore, we introduce “knowledge-driven” approaches, which complement data-driven methods by leveraging expert insights and domain knowledge to identify cases absent in training datasets. We then examine techniques and metrics for evaluating edge case detection methods, including detection performance, practical deployment (e.g., computational overhead), and domain-specific measures (e.g., crash rates and severity analysis). We conclude by highlighting key challenges for edge case detection, including data availability and quality issues, validation and interpretability limitations, the simulation-to-real gap, and computational constraints. The hierarchical classification and review of methods and assessment techniques in this survey enable modular and targeted testing frameworks by guiding the selection of detection methods for specific AV subsystems while considering methodological principles. It also supports practical testing by facilitating scenario generation in simulation and focused subsystem validation in the real world.
item.authors: Saeed Rahmani;Sabine Rieder;Erwin de Gelder;Marcel Sonntag;Jorge Lorente Mallada;Sytze Kalisvaart;Vahid Hashemi;Bart van Arem;Simeon C. Calvert;

item.title: A Review of Vision-Based Vehicle Detection for UAV-Based Traffic Monitoring: Experimental Insights and Future Directions
item.description: In Intelligent Transportation System (ITS), uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-based surveillance offers an innovative solution to traffic surveillance with wide coverage and real-time data collection capabilities. In comparison to fixed ground-based infrastructure, UAVs are able to respond to dynamic traffic but present challenges such as vehicle detection at varying altitudes, compensation for motion-induced image variations and efficient processing of high-resolution images. Deep learning has been largely beneficial on improving the detection accuracy; however, for practical deployment, a critical assessment of the accuracy, latency, and harmonization with current transportation systems needs to be carefully considered. This survey reviews recent advancements in the UAV-based traffic monitoring, with a primary focus being deep neural network models for traffic analytics in various urban settings. Three main challenges identified in the literature are ensuring compatibility with traffic control systems, achieving real-time processing to optimize traffic flow, and maintaining robust detection in different environmental conditions. Existing solutions often lack comprehensive frameworks for utilizing UAV captured data to respond to incidents and manage traffic effectively. Future research should focus on optimal detection models, edge processing, and adaptive control integration to improve the responsiveness of urban traffic management.
item.authors: Jianlin Ye;Christos Kyrkou;

item.title: Adaptive Neural Event-Triggered Control of Vehicular Platoons With Input Saturation Constraint and Unknown Disturbances
item.description: This article studies the problem of robust adaptive event-triggered control for connected vehicular platoon systems with input saturation constraint and unknown disturbances. First, the approximation identity of neural network is utilized to solve the unknown nonlinear functions. Then, based on constant time headway, the position tracking error and coupled sliding surface are constructed. Under backstepping recursion, the Lyapunov function is selected to develop auxiliary control functions. The adaptive event-triggered mechanism is developed to compensate for saturation effects through auxiliary control functions. The proposed control theory can reduce unnecessary transmission of communication resources and assure boundedness of the closed-loop system for all involved signals. And it guarantees that the Zeno behavior is eliminated. Finally, the feasibility of the presented method is justified with the simulation results.
item.authors: Yan-Jun Liu;Jiahui Wei;Hao Chen;Lei Liu;

item.title: Class-Enhanced Multi-Sampling and Multi-Level Graph Attention for 3-D Object Detection
item.description: Three-dimensional object detection is a key component of the perception module in autonomous driving systems. Compared to camera images, LiDAR point clouds provide richer spatial information, such as detailed structural and geometric cues of objects. However, existing 3D object detection methods face two major challenges: 1) loss of critical information due to downsampling or convolution operations, leading to missed detections, and 2) insufficient exploitation of contextual information around objects, resulting in inaccurate bounding box regression. These problems are particularly severe when detecting sparse point cloud objects that are distant or occluded. To address these issues, we propose two novel modules applicable to both point-based and voxel-based detection frameworks: the Class-Enhanced Multi-Sampling (CEMS) module and the Multi-Level Graph Attention (MLGA) module. The CEMS module employs an iterative class-aware sampling and semantic interpolation strategy to achieve more precise downsampling of critical information, while the MLGA module integrates both intra-layer and cross-layer graph attention to capture local geometric structures around objects as well as inter-object relationships, thereby enhancing the representation of key features. Comprehensive evaluations on multiple datasets, including ONCE, Waymo, and nuScenes, demonstrate that the proposed modules can consistently improve the detection performance across various network architectures while maintaining high inference efficiency.
item.authors: Xiangyang Wu;Jitao Pan;Qinglong Jiao;Kailun Qian;Zhen Liu;

item.title: 3-bit Transmission Mechanism-Based Adaptive Neural Path Following Control of 4DOF Underactuated USVs via Error-Constraint ILOS Approach
item.description: This paper investigates the path-following control problem for 4-degree-of-freedom (4DOF) underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) under internal/external uncertainties. The proposed control framework comprises the guidance and control modules. For the guidance subsystem, a novel error-constraint integral line-of-sight (EC-ILOS) method is originally developed to resolve the underactuation challenge. In the control subsystem, a virtual parameter learning-based adaptive neural network technique is proposed to counteract uncertainty impacts. To lighten the burden of data transmission in controller-actuator (C-A) channels, an innovative 3-bit transmission mechanism is designed, featuring a specialized encoder-decoder pair with a novel encoding strategy. The developed 3-bit transmission mechanism-based EC-ILOS adaptive neural control solution is endowed with two key advantages: 1) It achieves user-defined performance while eliminating parameter tuning difficulties in guidance systems; 2) It significantly reduces C-A channel data transmission through the new encoder-decoder mechanism. The Lyapunov stability theorem is used to analyze the convergence of all closed-loop system signals. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.
item.authors: Guibing Zhu;Junhui Li;Yong Ma;Zhixiong Li;M. Sotelo;

item.title: Multi-Modal Trajectory Prediction With Frenet Trajectory Translation
item.description: This paper presents a trajectory prediction algorithm called Frenet Trajectory Translation, which predicts future trajectories in the Frenet coordinate system conditioned on vehicle interactions, maps, and routes, all represented as graphs. Our method can accurately predict future motions by identifying distinct modalities derived from various routes and maneuvers. Additionally, since the predictions occur in the Frenet coordinate system, they inherently support multi-modality, allowing for generating counterfactual future trajectories based on diverse routing intentions. Additionally, we propose a novel modality sampling method to enhance the diversity of future motions and thus offer better modality coverage. Our algorithm has been tested across different roundabout locations, delivering state-of-the-art results. We conclude by integrating the Frenet Trajectory Translation with a downstream trajectory planner, showcasing combined prediction and planning outcomes in a simulated environment. The source code is available at https://github.com/studybox/FTT
item.authors: Boqi Li;Shaobing Xu;Huei Peng;

item.title: A Motion Planning Control Strategy for Autonomous Vehicles Considering Driving Style Personalization and Optimal Energy Consumption
item.description: This paper proposes a novel motion planning algorithm based on model predictive control (MPC) and fuzzy logic to address the coordinated motion planning problem in terms of optimal energy consumption while maintaining specific driving style. The MPC controller based on the linear time-varying (LTV) vehicle dynamics model is constructed to deal with the calculation of trajectory tracking accuracy, while the optimal energy consumption term is also integrated into the evaluation function. To transform the non-convex optimization problem into quadratic programming (QP), the tracking error is further linearized. Noting that differentiated control objectives lead to potential abnormal acceleration fluctuations, the weight adjustment mechanism is adopted to handle the adjustment of vehicle’s dynamic behavior. In the process of adaptive weight configuration, the fuzzy logic controller based on driving intention and deviation level is designed to achieve the goal of maintaining the preset driving style. Therefore, by leveraging the correlation between driving style definition and acceleration/deceleration decisions, the trade-off problem in motion planning and the riding comfort issue can be addressed simultaneously. Moreover, the improved algorithm under three different driving styles and the original MPC planner are tested and compared in the typical cornering scenario. By introducing the optimal energy consumption term at the cost of a 4.08% extension in scenario passage time, the proposed algorithm achieves up to a 29.76% reduction in trajectory deviation and a 38.89% decrease in approximate driving energy consumption. Visual analysis of driving objectives’ trade-off further indicates that different driving style presets lead to distinct optimization potentials, while trajectory tracking still plays a dominant role in the overall control objectives.
item.authors: Fuhao Zuo;Xia Li;Benxue Liu;

item.title: DriverPose: A Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Network for 3-D Driver Pose Estimation
item.description: In autonomous driving, the driver serves as the ultimate safety measure, making accurate pose estimation essential for effective driver monitoring systems. However, existing research on 3D human pose estimation has largely overlooked the important driving scenario. To address this, this work proposes DriverPose, a 3D driver pose estimation model based on a spatio-temporal convolutional network. DriverPose captures long-range sequential dependencies using temporal dilated convolutions and extracts spatial features through a novel graph attention mechanism. This mechanism integrates local and global information, uniquely embedding prior semantic knowledge of the driving context, such as kinematic hierarchies and common behavior patterns, to learn more relevant spatial relationships. Additionally, Conditional Batch Normalization with action type as a condition variable is applied after the graph convolution to adaptively handle different driving actions. To tackle the scarcity of training data in driving scenarios, a driving pose dataset named Human Driving-In-Vehicle (HDIV) with different driver body types and eight NDRTs is created. Experiments on the HDIV dataset and real-world driver videos show that DriverPose outperforms state-of-the-art methods in 3D driver pose estimation accuracy.
item.authors: Weicheng Zheng;Ruisheng Yuan;Zhenyu Zhang;Hui Zhao;Chengjie Wang;

item.title: Automated Parking Planning Based on Safety Corridor Constraints and Parking Space Matching
item.description: The field of Automated Valet Parking (AVP) has garnered significant academic interest in recent years. However, traditional parking planning methods often struggle with maneuvering in compact spaces and large-scale environments. While effective for short-distance parking, these methods frequently encounter increased computational latency and sub-optimal path lengths in long-distance parking scenarios. Fundamentally, the inherent complexity of large-scale facilities extends beyond the practical capacity of conventional single-stage planners, necessitating a multi-stage strategy to balance global search efficiency with local maneuverability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical parking planning framework using a decoupled two-stage approach. By integrating online safety corridor constraints with resolution-adaptive parking space matching, the method combines the global exploration of graph search with the local precision of optimization algorithms. The process employs a two-stage Hybrid A ${}^{\ast }$ strategy: global planning generates an initial trajectory in a low-resolution grid map, subsequently followed by local planning that refines the path to the target point within a high-resolution environment to ensure kinematic feasibility in constrained spaces. Experimental results indicate that this approach enhances algorithm efficiency by approximately 86.58% and reduces path length by an average of 21.68%. The proposed method improves adaptability to compact parking environments and reduces both generation time and path length in large-scale parking lots. Furthermore, the integration of adaptive safety corridor constraints and parking space matching enhances path safety and precision. The effectiveness of the method has been validated through real-world vehicle experiments, demonstrating its feasibility in practical AVP scenarios.
item.authors: Kai Liu;Jian Zhou;Haoran Li;Youchen Tang;Jinsheng Xiao;

item.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperation Scheduling Strategy for Single-Route Battery Electric Bus Fleets Considering Battery Capacity Decay and Nonlinear Charging
item.description: The scheduling problem of battery electric buses (BEBs) has been widely studied. However, most existing work focuses only on either operation or charging. In reality, these two aspects are interdependent and should be considered from a lifecycle perspective. This study proposes a cooperative scheduling strategy for BEB fleets on a single bus route. The strategy addresses opportunity charging under a limited charging infrastructure. It dynamically generates operation and charging decisions based on real-time system states. The goal is to reduce the impact of uneven terminal arrival times and mitigate battery aging. Both the nonlinear charging behavior and battery aging are considered in the charging plan. The BEB work cycle is modeled as two interrelated Markov Decision Processes (MDPs): one for operation and one for charging. A deep reinforcement learning framework, called the Double-SAC-Combination Framework, is used to solve the model. It integrates the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Discrete SAC algorithms. The model is validated using real-world data from Beijing Bus Line 44 (inner loop). Results show that the proposed strategy reduces daily battery capacity degradation by 8.5% to 33.3% compared to a no-control baseline. The best performance is achieved when the headway is 6 minutes, speed is 25 km/h, fleet size is 35, and there are 4 charging piles. Sensitivity analyses are conducted on BEB load differences, driving speed, headway, number of charging piles, fleet size, route length, and battery capacity.
item.authors: Qiang Feng;Yu Zhou;Honghai Li;Rui Feng;Bin Yu;

item.title: Risk Occupancy: A New and Efficient Paradigm Through Vehicle-Road-Cloud Collaboration
item.description: This paper proposes a novel 4D risk occupancy (RiskOcc) perception paradigm under the Vehicle-Road-Cloud integrated architecture, which unifies object detection and local mapping into a single representation spanning four dimensions: road-surface x and y coordinates, risk, and time. Distinct from conventional grid occupancy and risk field methods, this paradigm adopts an anchor-node-based perception approach with a concise yet reliable risk quantification scheme, enabling flexible and accurate capture of static and dynamic object occupancy states at current and future time steps, with per-occupancy-unit risk quantification. Compared with 3D-Occ, the proposed RiskOcc requires only one layer of data volume and achieves higher perceptual computational efficiency. Visualizations of risk occupancy perception results are presented based on the DAIR-V2X dataset, and a path planning method is developed to verify the usability of the risk occupancy map. Experimental results show that at an initial braking speed of 8 m/s, the model improves safety redundancy by 12.5% and reduces average deceleration by 5.41%, enhancing both safety and comfort. In summary, this study introduces a novel perception paradigm for intelligent connected vehicle (ICV), providing a compact and interpretable risk representation for cooperative perception and downstream planning in ICV systems.
item.authors: Jiaxing Chen;Wei Zhong;Bolin Gao;Yifei Liu;Hengduo Zou;Jiaxi Liu;Yanbo Lu;Jin Huang;Zhihua Zhong;

item.title: Blockchain-Assisted Reliable Federated Learning in 5G-Powered Vehicular Systems
item.description: The transformation of transport systems increasingly relies on connecting vehicles into cooperative networks, promising to reduce traffic congestion, lower emissions, and enhance road safety. Achieving these benefits requires efficient sharing of high definition (HD) map information across vehicles. Federated learning (FL) enables vehicles to collaboratively train shared models for HD maps, supporting accurate localization and dynamic environment understanding, without transferring raw data, thus preserving privacy. However, implementing FL in this context faces significant challenges: malicious participants can disrupt learning, and honest participants may disengage without sufficient incentives. To address these issues, we propose integrating a dual blockchain framework with FL, which evaluates participant reliability, weights contributions accordingly, and provides financial incentives to maintain engagement. This coordinated approach ensures that only trustworthy information contributes to HD map updates, preserving both data privacy and system integrity. By modeling and optimizing the system’s economic utility, and validating through simulations, we demonstrate that the framework is feasible under realistic settings when reward and subscription fees are appropriately calibrated, providing a robust foundation for secure, incentivized, and privacy preserving vehicular networks.
item.authors: Marcell Szabó;László Toka;

item.title: Virtual Coupled Train Set Intelligent Operation Control Method for High-Speed Railway Considering Carbon Emission Reduction
item.description: In this paper, we propose a virtual coupled train set intelligent operation control method for high-speed railway considering carbon emission reduction based on the Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework. Specifically, based on the theory of train dynamics, we consider the effects of slope, curvature, and tunnel conditions on the expected train spacing. Through analyzing the energy consumption of train operation, we take minimizing carbon emission reduction as one of the main control objectives and transform the virtual coupled train set intelligent operation control model into an optimal control problem. A real-world simulation experiment is conducted by using the Chengdu-Chongqing HSR as the background, we find that the model proposed in this paper performs effectively under line changing conditions, and can reduce a total of 0.72% of the traction carbon emissions of three follower trains. Finally, we compare the tracking errors and carbon emission reduction under three scenarios: different control objective weights (tracking and carbon emission), different time domains (predication and control), and different control strategies (moving block and virtual coupling). The results indicate that the proposed model requires a trade-off between tracking accuracy and carbon reduction effectiveness. To balance tracking precision and computational efficiency, it is recommended that the train’s horizon should not exceed 40. Compared to the moving block system, virtual coupling demonstrates outstanding advantages in terms of tracking interval and enhancing line capacity, and the proposed model can achieve a reduction of 2.81% in train traction carbon emissions.
item.authors: Baiquan Tai;Zhi Zhang;Wencheng Huang;

item.title: GeoLogistics Transformer: Exploring Urban Truck Traffic With Route-Adaptive Embedding and Contextual Logistics Graph
item.description: Accurate prediction of urban truck traffic is essential for efficient logistics and traffic management but remains challenging due to complex spatiotemporal dynamics. This study proposes the GeoLogistics Transformer (GLT), a forecasting model that integrates mobility patterns of different truck types, geographic context, and logistics attributes. Using truck trajectory data from Tokyo, GLT combines graph-based learning, temporal encoding, and Transformer-based spatial attention over grid tokens to capture both long-range logistics and temporal dependencies. Experimental results show that GLT achieves the highest explained variance at the immediate forecast horizon and consistently matches or outperforms benchmark models in mean absolute error (MAE) across longer horizons. The results highlight the importance of logistics-aware spatial modeling and truck type specific representations for urban truck traffic prediction.
item.authors: Gen Li;Jishi Wu;Zhongwei Luo;Tao Feng;Zongyuan Wu;

item.title: Integrity Monitoring of GNSS Railway Localization With a Map-Based Multipath Error Model
item.description: Satellite-based navigation can enable in the near future interoperable railway signaling capabilities and improve railway traffic management. For railway safety functions, the use of global navigation satellite system (GNSS) has to be proven safe for the specific operational environments. This is, however, still a challenge due to the presence of local GNSS errors, such as multipath, which are difficult to model. One of the main reasons is its strong dependency with the surroundings along the tracks that creates a high variability of the multipath error experienced by GNSS receiver at every point of the railway line. This work proposes a methodology to model the train GNSS multipath error by creating a digital map of multipath information. The information in the map provides a parametric and conservative description of the error that can be used by the GNSS receiver. The map-based error model is constructed by applying error overbounding techniques over empirical data collected along the tracks. The resulting error map is then integrated and evaluated in an advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) algorithm adapted to the railway environment and that provides a position solution along with associated integrity bounds. The experimental results based on real railway data demonstrate the capability of this methodology and models to provide a reliable multipath error description for train localization while maintaining high availability.
item.authors: Florian Rößl;Omar García Crespillo;

item.title: Real-Time Multiple Vehicle Tracking Based on Multivariate Trajectory Prediction With Encoder--Decoder LSTM in Varying Lighting Conditions
item.description: In this paper, we consider the problem of multiple vehicles tracking in different complex road scenarios using traffic surveillance videos captured by cameras in varying lighting conditions. We formulate the multiple object tracking problem as a vehicle trajectory prediction, where the goal is to generate a future trajectory sequence of the object in real-time. We propose a lightweight online multi-object tracker based on the Encoder-Decoder LSTM architecture which analyzes patterns underlying the past object trajectory and estimates the vehicle’s motion in subsequent frames. The goal of the developed method is to establish correspondences between vehicle objects within a sequence of video frames. The use of object motion features promotes the generation of high-quality object trajectories and operation in a constantly changing traffic scene environment, with varying traffic flow density and illumination conditions. Tracking results from vehicle trajectories can be used efficiently to estimate the traffic flow parameters, such as traffic volume, vehicle presence, and vehicle movement speed, leading to effective intelligent transportation system (ITS) deployment. To demonstrate the efficiency of the developed approach, the extensive numerical evaluation carried out on multiple traffic scene datasets under diverse conditions demonstrates significant and robust results. During experiments, the tracking performance of the method is measured using specialized MOT metrics against existing tracking algorithms. Our developed approach is competitive against existing resource-intensive trackers and achieves high HOTA and MOTA metrics on publicly available MOT benchmarks. The designed tracking module with an incorporated LSTM network runs at a frequency of 16 Hz, enabling real-time traffic flow monitoring.
item.authors: Igor Lashkov;Shanglian Zhou;Amanda Nitta;Guohui Zhang;

item.title: StructFormer: A Transformer-Based Multi-Structure Attention Model for Solving Routing Problems
item.description: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs), fundamental NP-hard challenges in intelligent transportation systems, often pose scalability challenges and require expert-dependent design when solved with traditional heuristics. Neural VRP solvers offer data-driven alternatives but suffer from limitations such as the “averaging effect” in self-attention, which impairs key-node differentiation and the modeling of salient structural relationships. Existing feature enhancement methods also overlook key structural patterns, limiting representation quality. To address these challenges, we propose StructFormer, a transformer-based improvement solver with multiview structural attention. Its core Multi-StructAttn module integrates multiview structural embeddings to mitigate the averaging effect, enhancing node differentiation and capturing salient structural relationships. Additionally, a global-centrality-based feature enhancement module embeds optimal connection patterns, enriching structural representation. A novel decoder further incorporates search-state-dependent dynamic heuristic information to improve step-wise decision-making during iterative refinement. Experiments on diverse TSP and CVRP benchmarks demonstrate that StructFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models. Furthermore, some modules of StructFormer are compatible with other learning-based solvers, offering significant performance gains on both TSP and CVRP.
item.authors: Longze Liu;Peilan He;Yanwei Yu;Guiyuan Jiang;Yidan Sun;Junyu Dong;Muwei Jian;Siew-Kei Lam;

item.title: Secure State Estimation of Nonlinear Autonomous Marine Vehicle Systems With Location-Varying Sparse Attacks
item.description: This paper investigates the secure state estimation problem of autonomous marine vehicles (AMVs) under location-varying sparse attacks and external disturbances, where the AMV is modeled as a continuous-time T-S fuzzy system. To effectively suppress destructive attacks, a redundant-channel transmission mechanism is adopted to transmit the measurable output information, and a necessary and sufficient condition for the reconstruction of the measurable outputs is given. Furthermore, the generalized inverse technique is applied to transform the original system into a form that is not affected by external disturbances, along with a necessary and sufficient condition for the observability of the transformed system. Then, an observer is designed using the reconstructed measurement output signals and the observable transformed system, which differs from the existing methods in that its estimation error can converge to zero in a finite time. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the designed observer are verified through simulation experiments.
item.authors: Qingdong Sun;Guang-Hong Yang;

item.title: DSTIGFN: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Interactive Graph Fusion Network for Traffic Flow Prediction
item.description: Accurate traffic flow prediction is crucial for the efficient management of urban transportation systems. However, existing models generally focus on modeling continuous traffic sequences, ignoring the multilevel correlation characteristics of spatio-temporal heterogeneity in traffic networks at different time scales. Moreover, the spatial dependencies among road nodes are usually modeled by static graphs, making it difficult to capture their dynamic evolution over time. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Interactive Graph Fusion Network. First, the model periodically encodes the original traffic flow sequence to extract the periodic patterns and global temporal structures embedded in it. Building on this foundation, a trend-preserving parity decomposition is applied to divide the time series into odd and even subsequences, preserving temporal trends while introducing diverse temporal perspectives to support multi-scale temporal modeling. For each subsequence, adaptive and supra-Laplacian graph structures are constructed to capture evolving spatial dependencies and deep temporal correlations. Graph convolution and a subgraph interaction fusion strategy are then employed to integrate complementary information across subsequences. Finally, by restoring the odd and even subsequence features to their original temporal order, the model effectively integrates global and local spatio-temporal dependencies, thereby enhancing its ability to predict complex traffic patterns. The source code is available at https://github.com/Zachary-Qi/DSTIGFN-master
item.authors: Shiqi Zhang;Zhen Liu;Yuzhuang Pian;Jialong Qian;Yonghong Liu;H. Oliver Gao;

item.title: Interpretable Symbolic Regression for Spatio-Temporal Traffic Prediction
item.description: Interpretable traffic prediction uncovers the dynamics of traffic variations in transportation networks, making it essential for accurate decision-making in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). However, widely-used methods, particularly those based on deep learning, often function as black-box models, limiting their interpretability and efficiency. To address this limitation, we propose an interpretable symbolic regression model for traffic prediction, StSr, achieving state-of-the-art performance while maintaining interpretability. Symbolic regression derives interpretable mathematical expressions directly from data, eliminating the need for predefined functional forms while employing gradient-free optimization to capture nonlinear relationships and perform feature selection, and fine-tune the free coefficients. Despite its generalizability, symbolic regression avoids abundant model structures, input, and reduces the computation complexity while maintaining excellent prediction performance. Notably, StSr leverages parallelism on CPUs to enhance computational efficiency and scalability, reducing reliance on GPU resources and making the model particularly effective for complex prediction tasks. The model’s novel end-to-end architecture comprises two key stages: the initial stage searches for the structure of prediction functions, and the subsequent stage optimizes the free coefficients within these structures. Discrete optimization is used for structure seeking, followed by continuous optimization for coefficient optimization. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through extensive experiments on various real-world traffic speed and flow datasets, demonstrating its ability to enhance performance and computational efficiency.
item.authors: Mingxi Li;Zhengmin Shi;Guoyang Qin;Wei Ma;

item.title: Robust Lateral Control of a Convoy of Autonomous and Connected Vehicles With Limited Preview
item.description: This paper investigates the lateral control of Connected and Autonomous Vehicle (CAV) convoys during lane change (LC) maneuvers in general and emergency lane change (ELC) maneuvers in particular. ELC maneuvers are initiated in response to emergency cues from either the front or rear of the convoy, enabling obstacle avoidance or facilitating the movement of other vehicles. The primary objective is to develop a lateral control strategy for CAVs leveraging inter-vehicular communication while not relying on position information from the road. This is particularly useful for lateral control of convoys when the road information is not readily available. A key assumption is the reliable connectivity among CAVs, allowing each vehicle to access GPS position traces from both the leading and immediate predecessor vehicles. This connectivity enables the construction of a composite LC trajectory, serving as a discretized preview of the desired trajectory. The proposed methodology entails trajectory construction, computation of cross-track, heading, and yaw-rate errors, and the formulation of a lateral control law. Furthermore, this paper assesses the robustness of the controller under varying longitudinal velocities and examines lateral string instability when lead-vehicle information is unavailable. Numerical results from sensitivity analyses and robustness tests demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed lateral control scheme for CAV convoys.
item.authors: Mengke Liu;Neelkamal Somisetty;Sivakumar Rathinam;Swaroop Darbha;

item.title: Lane-Changing Maneuver Prediction With Urban Arterial Traffic Data From Drones
item.description: This study addresses the challenge of predicting lane-change behavior in complex urban arterial environments, where interactions are heterogeneous and lane changing events are inherently rare. We propose Lane Change Direction and Timing Network (LC-DiTiNet), a Transformer-based framework that jointly predicts lane change direction and timing using an event-based formulation. To effectively handle the strong class imbalance between lane-keeping and lane changing events, we introduce a two-stage training strategy with focal loss, which stabilizes learning and improves performance on rare maneuvers. In addition, we propose a novel evaluation metric, the Driver Maneuver Prediction Index (DMPI), which integrates spatial (direction) and temporal (timing) accuracy through a normalized soft-DTW formulation, enabling a holistic assessment of maneuver prediction. Extensive experiments on drone-based urban traffic data demonstrate that the proposed model achieves robust performance across multiple prediction horizons, outperforming existing baselines particularly in long-horizon and minority-class scenarios. Furthermore, the model is computationally efficient, with approximately 2.02 million parameters and an inference time of 5.7 ms per vehicle, making it suitable for real-time intelligent transportation system (ITS) applications. These results highlight the effectiveness of jointly modeling maneuver direction and timing for capturing complex driver behavior in urban traffic.
item.authors: Sohyeong Kim;Pascal Frossard;Nikolas Geroliminis;

item.title: Accelerated Safety Evaluation for Autonomous Vehicles Using Markov Chain Score Ascent-Based Adaptive Importance Sampling
item.description: Before autonomous vehicles are deployed on public roads at scale, it is crucial to quantify their safety. The failure probability of the autonomous vehicle is a key metric for evaluating their safety. However, the rarity of risk scenarios makes existing closed box-based failure probability estimation algorithms expensive. To address this issue, we propose Markov Chain Score Ascent-based Adaptive Importance Sampling (MCSA-AIS) to accelerate the safety evaluation of the autonomous vehicles. MCSA-AIS minimizes the inclusive KL divergence between a parameterized proposal distribution and the optimal importance sampling distribution from the perspective of stochastic gradient descent. Since the gradient of the inclusive KL divergence is defined as an expectation over the optimal importance sampling distribution to be approximated, an unbiased gradient estimate is required. To overcome this issue, MCSA-AIS utilizes the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to generate some test scenarios that follow the optimal importance sampling distribution, then estimates the unbiased gradients of the inclusive KL divergence and improves the proposal distribution. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, We take two autonomous driving systems as the System Under Test (SUT) and evaluate their failure probabilities in test scenarios. Experiments demonstrate that, compared with the baseline testing algorithms, the proposed method significantly improves the sample efficiency and accuracy of failure probability estimation.
item.authors: Hao Wu;Yan Wu;Lifang Wang;Junzhi Zhang;

item.title: PanSR: An Object-Centric Mask Transformer for Maritime Panoptic Segmentation
item.description: Environmental panoptic perception and obstacle detection are key components in enabling autonomy for autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs). Recent studies have demonstrated that general panoptic methods, currently dominated by mask transformer approaches, are unsuitable for maritime environments, as they perform poorly in crowded scenes and in scenes with a wide range of object scales, highlighting the need for domain-specific panoptic methods. In this work, we identify several fundamental shortcomings of these recent methods and rethink architecture design choices from the perspective of perception for autonomous navigation. We introduce PanSR, a new panoptic segmentation method with the following main contributions: 1) an object-centric proposal extraction module for better handling of object size variety, 2) an improved ground-truth matching scheme consistent with proposal extraction, and 3) object-centric mask prediction for better instance separation of similar objects. With these enhancements, PanSR effectively mitigates instance merging, enhances small-object detection and increases performance in crowded scenes, delivering a notable +3.4% PQ improvement over state-of-the-art on the challenging LaRS benchmark and +8.4% PQ on WaterScenes, while retaining competitive performance on the autonomous driving perception benchmark Cityscapes. The code and models are publicly available on GitHub.
item.authors: Lojze Žust;Matej Kristan;

item.title: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control Under False Data Injection Attacks
item.description: Connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) are introduced to enhance the safety, efficiency, and mobility of transportation systems by leveraging advanced onboard sensors and wireless communication technologies. Cooperative adaptive cruise control (CACC), a fundamental application of CAVs, enhances adaptive cruise control (ACC) by treating multiple vehicles in close proximity as a platoon. Each vehicle within the platoon is equipped with a controller that leverages sensor-based measurements and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication to maintain safe and optimal inter-vehicle spacing. Although this system has significant potential to enhance traffic safety and efficiency, it remains vulnerable to false data injection (FDI) attacks, which can compromise system safety. Since the FDI attack is unknown and nonlinear, the CACC should be able to estimate and mitigate it in real-time. There exist several techniques in the literature to detect and estimate FDI attacks in real-time. However, none of them provides an asymptotic coverage. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel adaptive critic control and FDI attack estimation design leveraging reinforcement learning and Lyapunov stability analysis to mitigate the adverse effects of FDI attacks and bounded disturbance. This method yields semi-global asymptotic stability results. Theoretical analysis and simulation results are provided to illustrate the performance of the developed controller.
item.authors: Parisa Ansari Bonab;Arman Sargolzaei;

item.title: Analyzing the Impact of Service Stages on Demand and Modal Shift for Urban Air Mobility: A Case Study of Seoul Metropolitan Area
item.description: Upon the introduction of urban air mobility (UAM) services as a new transportation mode, a substantial portion of demand is expected to be generated by passengers shifting from conventional transportation modes. However, previous studies have focused on the primary mode of transportation that shifts to UAM in specific service stages, overlooking how modal shift patterns evolve as the service matures. Additionally, most prior studies have reported only total demand values, without distinguishing between different types of routes such as airport shuttles and local intra-city trips, which obscures route-specific demand characteristics. This study aims to bridge this gap by providing a comprehensive analysis of mode choice patterns and route characteristics for UAM services throughout the entire service stages. A utility-based mode choice model is applied, and a case study of the Seoul metropolitan area is conducted using empirical travel data. The results indicate that as UAM services mature, targeting the demand shift from private vehicle users has more potential to generate high demand than targeting public transport or taxi users. Furthermore, the findings indicate that routes with high demand during a specific service stage do not consistently follow high demand throughout the entire service stage. In particular, airport routes initially show higher modal shift rates due to greater time savings, their influence on overall UAM demand diminishes over time because of their inherently low traffic volume. These findings offer practical insights for policy-makers and planners, particularly in cities with mobility patterns similar to Seoul, by supporting strategic decisions on service planning and infrastructure development.
item.authors: Hyunsoo Kim;Kwanjung Yee;

item.title: W-Diffusion: A Probabilistic Generative Framework for Traffic Forecasting via Shallow Diffusion Mechanism
item.description: Timely-accurate traffic forecasting is crucial for urban traffic guidance and control. Accurate forecasting of traffic flow and speed are essential for analyzing road usage, alleviating congestion, and enabling real-time monitoring and dynamic navigation. These capabilities contribute to enhanced road safety and more efficient infrastructure operation. Most existing methods neglect the inherent uncertainties within the traffic scenario, which reduces their practicality for real-world traffic control. The newly emerged denoising diffusion probabilistic models bring new inspiration to address this issue. However, these models only involve a single generation process, which is not appropriate for traffic forecasting task. Furthermore, the impact of Gaussian noise in generative process brings more challenges for modeling signal correlations. To overcome these limitations, we present the first attempt to introduce the shallow diffusion mechanism into traffic forecasting task, leading to a novel framework called W-Diffusion. The proposed model consists of separated shallow and deep diffusion stages, in order to better capture the signal correlations during the generative process. We also devise a new denoising network AST-Unet, to combine the spatiotemporal learning capabilities of spatiotemporal graph neural networks with the uncertainty measurements of diffusion models. Comprehensive experimental evaluations are conducted on the Caltrans Performance Measurement System (PeMS) benchmarks to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.
item.authors: Zhepu Yang;Shuangxun Ma;Tao Dai;Peixin Chen;Ruixuan Zhang;Daniel Jian Sun;Xiangmo Zhao;Shirui Pan;

item.title: GPT-EV: Generative Pre-Training for Charging Demand Prediction of Electric Vehicle
item.description: While various machine learning techniques have been applied to charging demand prediction of electric vehicle (EV), existing methods lack a dedicated generative pre-training method capable of effectively capturing spatio-temporal dependencies in EV charging behaviors. This limitation hampers their generalization ability and prediction accuracy across diverse regions and time scales. To address this issue, this study proposes GPT-EV, a generative pre-training (GPT) method specifically designed for EV charging demand prediction. GPT-EV integrates an adaptive attention masking strategy to enhance the extraction of key temporal patterns, a customized spatio-temporal encoding mechanism to model intricate spatial-temporal relationships, and a decoder with probabilistic generation to improve robustness against uncertainties in charging behavior. These advancements enable the model to learn transferable representations, ensuring high-accuracy predictions across different regions and time scales even with minimal fine-tuning data. Experimental evaluations confirm that GPT-EV surpasses conventional deep learning and time-series GPT models across diverse regions and forecasting horizons, highlighting its potential to enhance mobility-aware energy management and integrated transportation-power planning.
item.authors: Tianjing Wang;Sheng Zhong;Shuqi Xie;Houbo Xiong;Zhao Yang Dong;

item.title: Multi-Tier Autonomous Ride Services: A Systematic Analysis of Fleet Providers' Pricing Strategies
item.description: This paper presents an analytical framework for optimal pricing and service design in multi-tier autonomous ride services, with premium and standard tiers, under monopoly and duopoly market structures. Users choose among tiers by jointly considering fares, expected wait times, and service quality, which leads to closed-form thresholds for premium–standard indifference, ride feasibility, and a critical impatience level that determines tier viability. The monopoly case is modeled as a three-stage Stackelberg game, which yields midpoint pricing rules and a condition under which a standard-only configuration maximizes profit when the premium cost markup is high. We analyze the duopoly case using the two-stage Bertrand (price competition) and Cournot (capacity competition) games, with unique equilibria characterized and comparative statics provided over trip distance, operating cost, cost ratio, and rider valuation. Results show that price competition increases user payoff, participation, and social welfare relative to Cournot and monopoly, while provider profit follows the opposite ordering (monopoly greater than Cournot greater than Bertrand). Multi-tier offerings can outperform single-tier strategies by endogenously segmenting riders when the gain from premium segmentation exceeds the associated cannibalization loss. A publicly observable Tesla–Waymo price snapshot is used as a real-world market illustration that provides preliminary empirical grounding for the model’s pricing insights, highlighting price-driven inclusion versus capacity- and cost-driven pricing. The framework yields threshold-based decision rules for when premium service is viable, when standard-only provision dominates, and how pricing responds to trip length, delay sensitivity, and operating cost.
item.authors: Daniel Mawunyo Doe;Xiangfang Li;Yuqing Hu;Zhu Han;Lijun Qian;

item.title: Passenger Trajectory Model and Passenger Movement Estimation System for Preventing Passenger Subway Door Accidents
item.description: Passengers being caught in subway doors can cause unexpected train delays and, in severe cases, serious injuries or loss of life. While previous studies have primarily focused on reactive methods that respond after passengers approach train doors, this study aims to proactively identify at-risk passengers before they reach the boarding area. We first develop a Passenger Trajectory Model (PTM) by analyzing the behavior of passengers descending stairs when a train is present at the station. Our analysis reveals that 97.85% of these passengers move directly toward the train doors, indicating that descending passengers are strong predictors of potential door-related incidents. Based on this behavioral insight, we propose a Passenger Movement Estimation System (PMES) that localizes passengers and classifies their movement types from single-frame Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) images. Three labeled datasets were constructed by annotating passengers into three movement classes: ascending, descending, and passing. The proposed PMES uses the YOLOv9 object detector for passenger localization and classification, while an ultra-lightweight custom architecture (SD-Net) enables efficient deployment. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves real-time performance with an mAP@0.5 of 97.58%. The framework is further validated across additional station environments with different layouts. Based on these results, we propose a Decision Support System (DSS) guideline to assist train operators in determining safe door-closing timing and suggest passenger-facing safety signage and alarm systems. The proposed framework can help reduce door-related accidents and minimize unexpected delays on subway platforms.
item.authors: Hee Jo;Yifan Li;Lisa Lim;Jo Woon Chong;

item.title: RT-RIDMOS: Real-Time Railway Intrusion Detection Method Based on Moving Object Segmentation
item.description: Railway intrusions, characterized by their unpredictable and sudden nature, pose a significant threat to operational safety in railway transportation. While recent breakthroughs in computer vision have substantially advanced intrusion detection algorithms, two fundamental challenges persist: the paucity of labeled intrusion samples, which severely constrains the performance and generalization of supervised models, and the limitation of existing methods to predefined object categories, rendering them ineffective against unknown threats. Therefore, this paper introduces RT-RIDMOS, an innovative real-time moving object segmentation method tailored for railway intrusion detection. At the input stage, the Spatio-Temporal Contextual Fusion (STCF) module equips the model with rich, multi-scale spatiotemporal information. This enables the network to segment intruding objects based on their motion discrepancy against the static background, rather than relying on appearance features. Consequently, our approach fundamentally circumvents the dependency on large-scale, category-annotated datasets, achieving robust, category-agnostic detection of arbitrary intruding objects. Furthermore, to satisfy the stringent real-time requirements for edge deployment while maintaining high performance, we have meticulously designed a lightweight backbone with a large receptive field. Extensive experiments on our custom-built, real-world railway intrusion dataset demonstrate the superiority of our method. With a remarkably low parameter count of only 1.12M, RT-RIDMOS achieves a state-of-the-art (SOTA) F-measure of 0.826. It significantly outperforms existing methods in model size, memory footprint, and inference speed, highlighting its considerable potential for continuous and efficient deployment on railway edge AI devices.
item.authors: Yongbo Wu;Ziyang Feng;Xinyu Zhu;Ping Tan;Huoping Yi;Jin Ding;Zhen Li;Jien Ma;

item.title: Low-Latency Object Detection in Driving Scenes: A Hybrid Spiking Neural Network for Motion-Compensated Fusion
item.description: Event camera recently is treated as a promising complementary visual sensor to overcome the perception challenges posed by complex lighting and high-speed traffic scenarios besetting the RGB cameras, and derives many event-RGB modality fusion approaches. However, the temporal synchronization between event streams and RGB frames is still a pending problem influencing on the high-performance and low-latency scene perception. In this work, we propose LOD-Drive, a hybrid spiking neural network for low-latency asynchronous object detection in driving scenes, which leverages the energy-efficient encoding capability of spiking neural networks (SNNs) to extract and maintain the high-frequency motion information from event streams. The spike-propagated motion features are asynchronously aligned with RGB motion flow for compensating the motion discrepancies within two modalities. Specifically, we propose a hybrid motion-guided temporal alignment module that encodes motion cues from event data to adaptively calibrate RGB features at the current timestamp, and the temporally aligned RGB features and event features are fused via a spatio-temporal cross-modal attention module with a decoder to output the final detections. Extensive experiment evaluations demonstrate that LOD-Drive significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on DSEC-Detection and PKU-DAVIS-SOD datasets.
item.authors: Zhonghui Han;Xinhao Luo;Jianwu Fang;Yuning Wang;Guoqi Li;Jianru Xue;

item.title: S2R: From Screening to Recognition, Event-Driven Perception of Railway Defects in Low-Power Systems
item.description: Automated, real-time inspection of railway infrastructure is critical for ensuring the safety of modern transportation systems. Deploying such perception systems on edge devices, however, is constrained by stringent power limitations. While Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are well-suited for low-power sensing, their non-differentiable spiking dynamics complicate direct training. In contrast, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) achieve easier optimization convergence but incur sustained high-power computational requirements, making them ill-suited for continuous and off-grid monitoring. Thus, integrating a shallow SNN for simple yet high-frequency tasks with a deep ANN for more complex tasks emerges as a promising solution. In this work, we propose an event-driven perception framework for railway surface defect segmentation to enable real-time railway defect inspection in edge deployments. The SNN serves as a region proposal module to detect potential defects, and only the defective segments are forwarded to the ANN for finer segmentation. This design enables our model to achieve high performance on sparse target inspection tasks with minimal energy consumption. We also collected and annotated a dataset named DeTian Railway Surface Defect (DTRSD), comprising 1,126 real-world railway defect images captured under diverse natural lighting conditions. These images capture anomalies, such as dust deposits and rust stains, offering a realistic environment for evaluating segmentation methods. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves competitive accuracy while reducing energy consumption relative to existing approaches. The code and dataset will be publicly available at https://github.com/lidadadaxu/HybridRSD
item.authors: Mingxu Li;Donghai Zhai;Shichun Wang;

item.title: Decentralized Learning for Multi-UAV Rail-Line Inspection With Imperfect Information: A Fictitious Self-Play Approach
item.description: Rail-line inspection is essential for the stable operation of rail transit systems. Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms are increasingly deployed for large-scale rail-line inspection, where efficient coordination and intelligent resource management are critical. However, most existing methods unrealistically assume complete global information and centralized control, which fails to hold in practical rail transit inspection scenarios where imperfect information arises from limited communication bandwidth and private UAV states. To address this challenge, we model the cooperative rail-line inspection problem as a stochastic game with imperfect information and propose a decentralized learning framework, termed Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle Fictitious Self-Play (U-FSP). Each UAV models its decision process as a belief-augmented Markov Decision Process (MDP) and iteratively learns equilibrium strategies through alternating best-response learning and policy averaging. We theoretically prove that the formulated rail-line inspection game constitutes an exact potential game, guaranteeing convergence of U-FSP to the Nash equilibrium. Simulation results in rail-line inspection environments demonstrate that U-FSP significantly reduces UAV energy consumption and task completion delay, mitigates resource congestion while maximizing overall rewards under imperfect information. Furthermore, analytical experiments show that U-FSP drives the rail-line inspection system toward a Nash equilibrium.
item.authors: Yin Jia;Li Zhu;F. Richard Yu;Bo Ai;Tao Tang;

item.title: Occlusion Handling for Intelligent Vehicles Using Audio-Visual Multi-Object Tracking
item.description: This paper proposes a novel multi-object tracking framework for intelligent vehicles, addressing the challenge of maintaining situational awareness during visual occlusions, where objects may be fully or partially blocked by other vehicles, infrastructure, or environmental elements. We first evaluate a visual-only tracking pipeline using static birth modeling and extend it with adaptive birth to compensate for missed detections; however, both approaches struggle to maintain tracks through occlusion events. Extending our previous work on audio–visual fusion, this study introduces a non-traditional, data-driven audio likelihood function that operates directly on raw microphone array signals in a track-before-detect (TBD) manner. Unlike conventional approaches relying on preprocessed direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimates, the proposed likelihood is computed using the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC)-based spatial spectrum analysis and formulated as a Gaussian mixture. Audio measurements are incorporated into a Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) implementation of the Labeled Multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filter, and the resulting visual and audio posteriors, obtained after independent LMB updates, are fused using Generalized Covariance Intersection (GCI). A physics-based simulation framework is developed to generate realistic vehicle acoustic signals and evaluate performance under two urban traffic scenarios with varying interaction density (moderate and dense). Monte Carlo experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves tracking accuracy, cardinality estimation, and robustness compared to visual-only baselines. The results highlight the effectiveness of signal-level audio–visual fusion in maintaining track continuity under prolonged occlusions and increased scene complexity.
item.authors: Thushara R. Bandara;Amirali K. Gostar;Prarthana Abeysinghe;Ehsan Asadi;Reza Hoseinnezhad;

item.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization for Location-Inventory-Allocation and Evacuation Planning Under Demand and Facility Disruption Uncertainties in Humanitarian Logistics
item.description: We investigate an integrated location-inventoryallocation and evacuation planning problem in disaster response, considering uncertainties in both the disruption ratios of distribution centers (DCs) and rescue shelters (RSs) and the demand of affected individuals for relief materials. Unlike conventional models that assume complete facility failures, our approach allows partially functional capacities at disrupted facilities. To capture these complexities, we develop a two-stage adaptive distributionally robust (TADR) optimization model. The first stage involves decisions regarding the locations of DCs, RSs, and backup warehouses (BWs), along with prepositioning inventory levels at DCs and BWs, prior to the realization of uncertain demand and facility disruption ratios. The second stage determines the allocation of relief materials from DCs and BWs to RSs and the evacuation planning for affected individuals from disaster areas to RSs, once these actual uncertainties are observed. To exactly solve the model, we reformulate it into a computationally tractable form and develop a customized Benders decomposition (BD) algorithm, incorporating two acceleration strategies to improve solution efficiency. The robustness and adaptability of our model and algorithm are validated through numerical experiments using randomly generated instances and realworld data from the Luding earthquake in China. The results demonstrate that: (i) The TADR model yields more reliable and flexible rescue plans compared to stochastic and deterministic benchmarks; (ii) The proposed algorithm achieves high computational efficiency; and (iii) Integrating BWs into the relief network plays a vital role in improving operational efficiency and reliability.
item.authors: Xueting Feng;Dujuan Wang;Yunqiang Yin;T. C. Edwin Cheng;Dunhu Liu;

item.title: Act Natural! Naturalistic Projection for Traffic Analysis in Multimodal Behavior Scenarios
item.description: Autonomous agents operating in traffic environments must consider how their behaviors might affect the human drivers around them, even when not directly interacting with them. To this end, it is often beneficial to be predictable and appear naturalistic. Existing methods for this purpose use human actor intent modeling or imitation learning techniques, but these approaches rarely capture all possible motivations for human behavior and/or require significant amounts of data. Our work extends a technique for modeling unimodal naturalistic behaviors with an explicit convex set representation, to account for multimodal behavior by using multiple convex sets. This more flexible representation provides a higher degree of fidelity in data-driven modeling of naturalistic behavior that arises in real-world scenarios in which human behavior is, in some sense, discrete, e.g. whether or not to yield at a roundabout. Equipped with this new set representation, we develop an optimization-based filter to project arbitrary trajectories into the set so that they appear naturalistic to humans in the scene, while also satisfying vehicle dynamics, actuator limits, etc. We demonstrate our methods on real-world human driving data from the inD (intersection) and rounD (roundabout) datasets.
item.authors: Hamzah I. Khan;David Fridovich-Keil;

item.title: Bi-Level Auction-Based Platoon Control for Signal-Free Intersections
item.description: This study presents a bi-level auction-based framework for coordinated platoon control at signal-free intersections, leveraging the capabilities of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication. Unlike traditional road pricing mechanisms, which lack individual differentiation and responsiveness to local congestion, the proposed framework enables dynamic and equitable traffic management by incorporating vehicle-level valuations of travel time. At the upper level, vehicle requests are grouped in non-conflicting movements, and a Sponsored Search Auction (SSA) determines the priority sequence based on individual bids and proximity to the intersection. At the lower level, an optimization model jointly determines the optimal platoon speeds and lengths, allowing for platoon splitting when necessary. A mixed-integer nonlinear formulation is developed and relaxed for efficient solution. The proposed mechanism ensures efficiency and fairness, addressing the coordination challenges arising from heterogeneous platoon preferences. Integrated into the SUMO microscopic simulation platform, the framework demonstrates significant improvements in intersection efficiency and equity compared to conventional methods, offering a scalable and adaptive approach to traffic coordination in CAV-only environments.
item.authors: Christina Iliopoulou;Emmanouil Kampitakis;Eleni I. Vlahogianni;

item.title: Predefined Time Cooperative Control Strategy for Multi-Vectored Water-Jet Robots Transport Using Unknown Payload Dynamics
item.description: To address these cooperative transport challenges of multiple underwater robot systems (MURs) in densely cluttered underwater environments, such as model uncertainties, external disturbances, and unknown payload dynamics, this paper proposes a predefined time cooperative transport strategy. First, a payload centered local gradient based trajectory generation method for traversing narrow passages. Second, we develop a predefined time disturbance observer (PTDO) to estimate the disturbances, and payload forces. The PTDO provides feedback to the controller while ensuring that the estimation error converges to a bounded value within a predefined time. Finally, a predefined time backstepping based tracking controller (PTC) is developed such that the tracking errors enter a prescribed residual set within a user assigned time bound, and this bound is independent of the initial conditions. The Lyapunov stability theory and simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed strategy in cooperative payload transport tasks.
item.authors: Lei Wang;Huiming Xing;Yong Gao;Chunying Li;Shuxiang Guo;Guangchun Li;

item.title: Dwelling and Speed Advisory Enhanced Max-Pressure Control With Transit Signal Priority
item.description: Max-Pressure (MP) control is a decentralized real-time traffic signal control method that is popular for its simplicity and theoretical stability. However, most existing MP controllers prioritize throughput for private vehicles without accounting for the specific needs of transit services that are essential for sustainable urban mobility. This oversight can exacerbate transit delays and undermine the effectiveness of public transportation systems. To address these challenges, this study introduces a Priority-MP framework that integrates transit signal priority and driver advisory systems into MP control for multi-modal traffic networks. By weighting pressures based on real-time vehicle occupancy and considering more realistic scenarios that account for the presence of transit stations, Priority-MP prioritizes high-occupancy transit vehicles while ensuring network queue stability. In addition, the framework integrates driver advisory systems to provide speed and dwell time recommendations for transit vehicles. Experiments on a real-world multi-modal traffic corridor in Amsterdam show that compared to existing MP control methods: 1) Priority-MP highlights an important trade-off: it significantly reduces average passenger delay by prioritizing high-occupancy transit vehicles, even though this may lead to increased average vehicle delay when the impact of transit stations are ignored; 2) Priority-MP considering transit stations reduces both vehicle delay and passenger delay while maintaining the network stability; and 3) Priority-MP integrating driver advisory systems further improves the travel smoothness of transit vehicles by reducing transit queuing counts.
item.authors: Chaopeng Tan;Georgios Laskaris;Dingshan Sun;Robin Abohariri;Marco Rinaldi;Hans van Lint;

item.title: Guest Editorial Introduction to the Joint Special Issues on Advanced Air Mobility Integration Into Multimodal Transportation Systems
item.description: null
item.authors: Hamsa Balakrishnan;Husni R. Idris;Max Z. Li;Hani S. Mahmassani;Craig R. Wanke;

item.title: Urban-Rural Bus-Assisted Drone Logistics Delivery With Time Window Considerations
item.description: With the rapid growth of the e-commerce industry, the demand for parcel delivery in rural areas has been increasing year by year. However, long delivery distances and sparse population distribution make it difficult for traditional logistics providers to offer cost-effective services. To improve delivery efficiency by leveraging existing transport resources, this paper proposes a multi-visit bus-assisted drone routing problem considering customer points with soft time windows, called MV-BDRP-STW, which leverages urban-rural buses to assist drones in logistics distribution, combining the flexibility of drones with the accessibility of the bus system. The problem includes the following key components: 1) Multiple buses depart from the same station, each carrying a drone for logistics tasks, with drones launched and collected at bus stations; 2) Customer points are considered with soft time windows, and a penalty function is applied; and 3) Drones can serve multiple customer points in a single flight. We formulate the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and develop a two-stage heuristic algorithm to solve small- and large-scale instances with data based on real-world scenarios. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and show significant cost reductions under different operational settings.
item.authors: Yu Jiang;Chen Guo;Ye Yuan;Mengmeng Liu;Qingwen Xue;

item.title: Reinforcement Learning Approach for Traveling Salesman Problem With Drones in Dynamic Environment
item.description: The truck-drone collaborative systems in last-mile delivery can improve the flexibility and efficiency of logistics delivery, where the drones are not limited to the road traffic conditions. The Traveling Salesman Problem with Drones (TSP-D), which requires routing optimization of a heterogeneous fleet of vehicles in coordination, has become a vital problem to be solved. Most existing models tend to improve the delivery efficiency, considering the battery capacity and load limit of drones. In fact, the effect of dynamic environment is also important for TSP-D to be applicable in the real world. Therefore, the paper introduces additional challenges to traditional TSP, including truck-drone coordination, traffic variation and dynamic delivery demand, which complicate the optimization process and require robust and adaptive solution methods. We propose a Dynamic Reinforcement Learning for Truck-Drone Delivery (DRTDD) method integrating attention-based encoder-decoder to solve the TSP-D in dynamic environment. The state space of the DRTDD, encompassing vehicle status, dynamic demand information, and time-varying vehicle speeds, is updated at each time step, enabling the MDP to generate optimal routing decisions for both the truck and the drone. The method has been validated within the complex Shanghai freight transport network and real logistics dataset. This study offers an innovative method in the field of vehicle-drone coordinated routing optimization, with reinforcement learning to deal with traffic variation and dynamic delivery demand. It can help to establish a framework for future research on optimizing logistics and delivery systems in increasing complex and dynamic environment.
item.authors: Qingwen Xue;Yu Jiang;Ye Yuan;

item.title: Integrated Network Design and Demand Estimation for Advanced Air Mobility Using an Extended Multiple-Allocation p-Hub Median Framework
item.description: It is essential to take the emerging transportation mode, Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), into transportation planning for developing a safe and efficient integrated multimodal transportation system. However, there are many operational uncertainties of AAM due to technological advancements, industry development, and regulatory establishment. Instead of operational details, e.g., fleet planning, eVTOL scheduling, and passenger assignment, transportation planners and policymakers want to know potential vertiport locations and the number and spatial distribution of travelers shifting from driving to using AAM services. To address these needs, our study examines the AAM integrated network design and demand estimation from a planning perspective. Given a traffic analysis zone (TAZ)-level origin and destination (OD) demand matrix, we propose an Extended Multiple Allocation p-Hub Median Problem (E-MApHMP) to determine optimal vertiport locations and estimate the shifted demand simultaneously. The objective of the mathematical programming is to minimize system-wide generalized travel cost, or, equivalently, to maximize the savings in generalized travel cost from shifting ground demand to air. A case study of Tampa Bay Region Plus (TBR+) involves 1,526 TAZs across seven counties, assuming each TAZ could potentially host one vertiport. Given the complexity of the problem, we developed a three-part chromosome-structured Genetic Algorithm (GA) with local search strategies to solve it efficiently. The traveler and socioeconomic data for this paper were drawn from a travel demand model developed for western Florida, US. Across multiple problem instances with fixed initial seeds, the proposed genetic algorithm (GA) consistently outperformed other metaheuristic algorithms and the Gurobi solver in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. A factorial design sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify key parameters influencing AAM demand, the share of low-income travelers, and access and egress travel distances to vertiports. Results from the Type II ANOVA indicate that vertiport processing time, vertiport parking price, and the per-mile flying fee are the most significant factors affecting these outcomes.
item.authors: Mahdi Monemi Nodehi;Yantong Dou;Joseph Post;Yu Zhang;

item.title: Evaluating Multi-Modal UAM Impacts at Metro Region Scale: A San Francisco Bay Area Study
item.description: This paper presents a method for evaluating and analyzing the effect of multi-modal Urban Air Mobility (UAM) operations on passenger travel time and the ground transportation system in a metropolitan region. The proposed method comprises a vertiport network design module, a graphical-processing-unit-based (GPU-based) micro-simulator for modeling vehicle movements, and a UAM allocator. We perform a hierarchical vertiport network design to determine vertiport placement and passenger assignment. With an ultra-fast parallelized micro-simulator, we simulate passenger movement and measure changes in traffic network congestion in the presence of UAM operations. We apply the proposed method to 9 million driving trips, representing roughly half-day demand in the San Francisco Bay Area, and estimate UAM and non-UAM passenger travel time changes by providing UAM service. Assuming that passengers use UAM if there is a travel time saving, the results showed a reduction of up to 37.07% of total Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT). The changes in the average travel speed of the road network and the travel time of non-UAM passengers also showed a reduction in ground congestion, although with a significant number of vertiports. An infrastructure analysis to better understand the comparative value of the land showed that UAM, as part of a multimodal system, could move more people per unit of land area compared to existing urban land-based transit options in the study region.
item.authors: Xin Peng;Xuan Jiang;Vishwanath Bulusu;Emin Burak Onat;Raja Sengupta;
